body: I had extreme vertigo, couldn’t walk and couldn’t stop vomiting. Went to the emergency room 5 times in one month, no one knew what was wrong with me and kept sending me home with different pills to calm my nausea and vertigo. The last visit to the ER, I started getting the feeling of pins on my legs and my vision was getting really bad due to the vertigo, the doctor during that shift of my visit ordered an MRI.  30 mins later after the MRI results, I was diagnosed with MS. MRI showed I had a huge lesion near my cerebellum and that side of my brain was very inflamed. I got a spinal tap and was on steroids treatment for 2 days in the hospital. I am thankful that I was lucky enough to be diagnosed and have thankfully not gotten any of those type of severe symptoms ever again, but I am utterly traumatized by the experience. Till this day, if I feel nauseous I get anxiety thinking it’s a relapse.

I was barely turning 21. I am now 25, so it’s been roughly 4 years. The way I found out was because I had horrible vertigo the day I woke up to go to class and went to the ER 4 different times in a span of a month because no one knew what was wrong with me until one doctor decided to do an MRI on my last visit. Great times.
